scope: All originalEN namedreferences, not an identitymerge of namesakes.

references.text: A regular you haven’t seen for a while… Myrtille.
MYRTILLE: “Well, hello there! I wasn’t sure you’d received my message.”
MYRTILLE: “Are you going to get going, or what?”
MYRTILLE: “To the shelter in Montreuil. Thanks.”
MYRTILLE: “Damn, it feels good to be warm!”
MYRTILLE: “And uh… speaking of being warm… things are kind of tough, right now. Moneywise, if you know what I mean...”
“Myrtille… You know it’s always free for you.”
MYRTILLE: “No way. Forget it. I’m a passenger just like any other.”
MYRTILLE: “Let’s make a deal instead, ok? An agreement, that is.”
MYRTILLE: “I’ll tell you a riddle and if you find the solution, I’ll pay the fare. Sound good?”
You catch sight of Myrtille sitting on the sidewalk.
MYRTILLE: “Brrr… It’s cold as hell out there!”
MYRTILLE: “Montreuil, please. You know the ropes.”
MYRTILLE: “We make a good team, the two of us...”
MYRTILLE: “Even though you always win…”
MYRTILLE: “But anyhow, it’s not like you cost me that much…”
MYRTILLE: “Even though you keep fleecing me…”
MYRTILLE: “Even though I keep fleecing you!”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, you ‘member our little arrangement, dontcha?”
“Of course. I remember it, Myrtille.”
MYRTILLE: “Good. If you answer my riddle, I pay for the ride. If you don’t…”
MYRTILLE: “Are you listening? Ready?”
MYRTILLE: “When you have me, you want to share me, but if you do share me, you don't have me.”
MYRTILLE: “Of course that’s it. What are you expecting, a novel or something!”
MYRTILLE: “When you have me, you want to share me, but if you do share me, I don’t exist… Well?”
MYRTILLE: “And it’s all mine. I worked it out all by myself...”
MYRTILLE: “…with my own little brain.”
MYRTILLE: “Mayonnaise? You gotta be kidding me — mayonnaise!”
MYRTILLE: “I’m gonna give you a second try.”
“Aw, come on, Myrtille! You’ve got me over a barrel. I just don’t know.”
MYRTILLE: “Answer my riddle. When you have me, you want to share me, but if you do share me, I don’t exist.”
Myrtille shakes her head slowly, left to right.
MYRTILLE: “Poor little thing! You really don’t get it, do you?”
MYRTILLE: “It’s a secret!”
MYRTILLE: “I only exist if… you don’t share me: I’m a secret!”
“Well done, Myrtille. Good job.”
MYRTILLE: “Damn, right. I’m not just a babe, you know. I’m damn smart, too.”
“It’s a good riddle, Myrtille.”
MYRTILLE: “You like it?”
MYRTILLE: “Well then, what’s your answer?”
MYRTILLE: “I only exist… if I’m not shared. What am I?”
MYRTILLE: “A smile?”
MYRTILLE: “Ha! A lie!”
MYRTILLE: “Did you say… sleep?”
MYRTILLE: “No way!”
MYRTILLE: “The answer is ‘a secret’!”
MYRTILLE: “If you share a secret, it’s no longer a secret…”
MYRTILLE: “Well then, aren’t you a smart one.”
MYRTILLE: “Yeah, a secret. If you share it, it’s no longer a secret. So, there you go.”
MYRTILLE: “I sure as hell found that one out the hard way, handsome.”
MYRTILLE: “All those goddamn whores, a bunch of bitches who pretended to be shocked when they heard I’d lost everything — my boyfriend, the roof over my head, my entire life…”
MYRTILLE: “So what did they go and do next, huh?”
MYRTILLE: “Fuck! They blabbed it all over town. Told everything… to everyone. No secret there, that’s for sure.”
MYRTILLE: “So I couldn’t get a job anymore, and I lost every goddamn last thing.”
MYRTILLE: “That’s all the past now. I forgave those stupid bitches.”
MYRTILLE: “That’s what I learned out on the street: forgiveness.”
A few minutes later, you get to the shelter where Myrtille is going to spend the night.
MYRTILLE: “So, anyhow, since you guessed my riddle…”
MYRTILLE: “No problem, handsome.”
MYRTILLE: “Awww! You’re a sweetheart… I’ll make it up to you, promise.”
MYRTILLE: “Well then, since you didn’t answer my riddle… I guess the ride’s on you tonight.”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, I’m off… See you soon, handsome.”
MYRTILLE: “Don’t worry, I’m gonna give you an easy one this time…”
MYRTILLE: “I’m nothing, but you can create me. You can’t see me, yet I’m all around. What am I?”
MYRTILLE: “Like I said. It’s an easy one. I’ll give you a minute or two.”
MYRTILLE: “So, what do you say?”
MYRTILLE: “Absence? Sorry, numbskull, wrong answer!”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, if you ask me, absence is something you can definitely see. Those two missing molars of mine back there… believe me, I can see ‘em!”
MYRTILLE: “ …”
MYRTILLE: “You’re good.”
MYRTILLE: “That’s the right answer. Emptiness.”
MYRTILLE: “Wrong answer, sorry.”
MYRTILLE: “Did you just say… salami?”
MYRTILLE: “You must be hungry then. It’s the same with me. Food on the brain whenever I’m hungry. It’s awful.”
MYRTILLE: “But that’s not the answer. Not even close.”
MYRTILLE: “It’s emptiness. The right answer is emptiness.”
MYRTILLE: “We can create it, can’t see it, it’s all around us, up there in the sky… You know, in outer space.”
MYRTILLE: “What d’ya mean? That I’m too dumb to know the Earth revolves around the Sun, and that all that stuff is suspended out there in emptiness?”
MYRTILLE: “Thanks. That means a lot to me.”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, I’m not gonna lie. I didn’t make that one up.”
MYRTILLE: “This guy who volunteers at the shelter told me it.”
MYRTILLE: “The guy’s a real brain. Talk about a brain! An astro… something or other. And not an astrologer, right? A real profession.”
MYRTILLE: “Yup. A decent guy.”
MYRTILLE: “Anyway, we’re almost there.”
MYRTILLE: “You sure know a lot about space for a taxi driver.”
“Thanks, Myrtille.”
MYRTILLE: “I was just joking, you know. I don’t believe ‘em for a second, all those political hacks going on about... what do they call it?”
MYRTILLE: “Oh right, COMMON GROUND. For each of us, there’s a goddamn common ground.”
MYRTILLE: “Bullshit! Bunch of assholes, those guys.”
MYRTILLE: “As if anybody was interested in my little corner of the universe.”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, I wouldn’t know a goddamn thing about all that, eh?”
MYRTILLE: “Why should I? Don’t even know where I’m going to sleep most nights… so the orbit speed of some goddamn planet…”
MYRTILLE: “Screw that!”
MYRTILLE: “You better pull over here. Don’t like getting out of a taxi in front of ‘em all.”
MYRTILLE: “It’s not you, big guy. It’s just that, people ask questions after. They spread rumors, like I’m blowing you for free cab rides.”
MYRTILLE: “I don’t like being taken for a whore. It gives the other guys ideas.”
MYRTILLE: “Hey! Don’t get me wrong, handsome!”
MYRTILLE: “You’re a sweetheart, handsome.”
MYRTILLE: “Here you go. You definitely earned it.”
You take the money. In the rearview mirror, disappointment flashes across Myrtille’s face.
MYRTILLE: “Well, then… I’m off.”
“No thanks, Myrtille. We’re good.”
MYRTILLE: “You don’t have to… to do that.”
“I’m happy to, Myrtille.”
MYRTILLE: “You can be a real pain sometimes, you know.”
MYRTILLE: “You didn’t guess right… so… I’m outta here. Always good to see you, handsome.”
MYRTILLE: “Salami, my foot!”
Myrtille and her shopping bag exit the cab. The slam of the car door rings in the cold night air.
MYRTILLE: “I told ‘em a good one yesterday. Nobody figured it out…”
MYRTILLE: “Not too surprising, though, is it? It’s not like the guys I run into are geniuses or anything…”
MYRTILLE: “Then again, some of ‘em probably took my little riddle the wrong way…”
MYRTILLE: “Listen up…”
MYRTILLE: “My pocket is empty and yet there’s something in it!”
MYRTILLE: “You see why the other guys didn’t like it too much?”
MYRTILLE: “Because of the empty pockets. They know all about them!”
MYRTILLE: “You shoulda seen the look on their faces when I told ‘em the answer…”
MYRTILLE: “Hey, wait a second! You have to get the answer all by yourself.”
MYRTILLE: “I’ll tell you the riddle one more time, in case you weren’t listening like you shoulda been: ‘My pocket is empty, but there’s something in it!’”
MYRTILLE: “Go ahead. I’m listening.”
MYRTILLE: “Well then? What do you say?”
MYRTILLE: “What the…? How did you guess?”
“Well… I just thought it over, Myrtille.”
MYRTILLE: “You’re good!”
MYRTILLE: “Or maybe it’s ‘cuz you have a hole in your pocket, that’s how come you figured it out so fast!”
MYRTILLE: “That’s right! ... Well, ok… Good job!”
MYRTILLE: “So why are you a taxi driver then?”
MYRTILLE: “Yeah, yeah, yeah. That’s right!”
MYRTILLE: “No, serious. I’m just messin’ with you! You’re a smart one, that’s all.”
MYRTILLE: “Nah, forget it! I’m just messin’ with you… I know you weren’t born yesterday.”
MYRTILLE: “Good job, handsome.”
MYRTILLE: “That’s not it… not even close.”
MYRTILLE: “Aah! Sure feels good, ‘cuz you ain’t no fool!”
MYRTILLE: “You give up?”
MYRTILLE: “Pfft. What a poor sport. It’s too bad…”
MYRTILLE: “The right answer is, mister smarty pants… a hole!”
MYRTILLE: “A hole in a pocket is empty, but it’s a thing, too! Get it?”
“Yeah, sure. I get it, Myrtille.”
MYRTILLE: “I like that riddle. It kinda comforts me.”
MYRTILLE: “‘Cuz that way, I says to myself, I always got somethin’ in my pocket.”
But it’s not about modesty. You know her well — there’s not a modest bone in Myrtille’s body.
MYRTILLE: “Tonight, the ride’s on you!”
MYRTILLE: “Here you go.”
MYRTILLE: “You sure?”
“I’m saying so because I am sure, Myrtille.”
MYRTILLE: “I… Thank you, for everything.”
MYRTILLE: “I hope you're ready tonight. I’ve got a tough one…”
MYRTILLE: “I’m everywhere to be seen, yet nowhere in between. Climb as you may, I’ll run farther away.”
MYRTILLE: “What am I?”
MYRTILLE: “So? How do you like it?”
MYRTILLE: “One of my… girl pals told it to me. Have I ever mentioned Simone?”
MYRTILLE: “Simone was, well… like a sister.”
MYRTILLE: “We met on the street. We’d run into each other at the shelter in the 16th every now and then, before those rich bastards kicked us out.”
MYRTILLE: “Scumbags, all of ‘em. Let me tell you, if I were king…”
MYRTILLE: “I’d give ‘em the guillotine.”
MYRTILLE: “Simone, she’s the one who got me into riddles. She did crossword puzzles, too. Stuff to improve your mind.”
MYRTILLE: “She was good.”
MYRTILLE: “She moved south. Better for her health, she said. Needed to look for new horizons.”
MYRTILLE: “But me and her, we were constantly fighting in the end. She was a nasty piece of work. A real bitch.”
MYRTILLE: “And she stole some of my stuff, too.”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, here we go. The riddle.”
MYRTILLE: “I’m everywhere to be seen, yet nowhere in between. Climb as you may, I’ll run farther away. What am I?”
MYRTILLE: “Right! I’m so busy blabbering away, I almost forgot — we’re not here just to smell the roses.”
MYRTILLE: “But there was something not quite right about her. She was always trying to be the best.”
MYRTILLE: “But surviving on the streets isn’t about outdoing the other guy — it’s about outsmarting him.”
MYRTILLE: “Or her!”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, enough about Simone! You still haven’t answered the riddle…”
MYRTILLE: “I’m everywhere to be seen, yet nowhere in between. Climb as you may, I’ll run farther away.”
MYRTILLE: “Well, what am I?”
MYRTILLE: “Tick…”
Words like “elevator” or “dumbwaiter” aren’t Myrtille’s style. So it can’t be that.
MYRTILLE: “Tick…”
MYRTILLE: “Tick…”
MYRTILLE: “Tock!”
MYRTILLE: “Gimme your answer, handsome!”
MYRTILLE: “An elevator?”
MYRTILLE: “Not at all, handsome. Not — At — All!”
MYRTILLE: “It’s ‘horizon’. Horizon is the right answer.”
MYRTILLE: “The Earth? I don’t get it...”
MYRTILLE: “The right answer is ‘horizon’, handsome. Not ‘Earth’.”
MYRTILLE: “You’re a weird one at times, you are…”
MYRTILLE: “The Earth!”
MYRTILLE: “That’s it!”
MYRTILLE: “I can’t believe it… Goddamn, you’re good!”
MYRTILLE: “Honestly. Good job, man!”
Suddenly, there’s a faraway look on her face. Perhaps she’s thinking about Simone?
MYRTILLE: “The horizon…”
MYRTILLE: “I hate it when you gimme that… You didn’t even try!”
MYRTILLE: “I know what you’re up to. You’re playin’ Mr. Nice Guy so I won’t have t’pay.”
MYRTILLE: “Did you know that, the higher we climb, the farther away the horizon is? Like, you can see a lot farther at the top of the Eiffel Tower than you can at the bottom?”
MYRTILLE: “Personally, I don’t get it.”
MYRTILLE: “I never been up there anyhow.”
MYRTILLE: “So what’s it like?”
You can make out Myrtille’s shelter at the end of the street.
MYRTILLE: “Yeah, I guess so…”
MYRTILLE: “But I’m not so sure I wanna see Paris from up there anyhow.”
MYRTILLE: “Course, the smell of piss mustn’t be so bad. But, I dunno. It’s like…”
You pull into an empty space, and Myrtille clutches her shopping bag close to her chest.
MYRTILLE: “A promise is a promise… and all that jazz.”
“Thanks, Myrtille, but you keep the money. Like I said, it’s on me.”
MYRTILLE: “But…”
MYRTILLE: “You didn’t have to do that, handsome. You’re a good guy.”
Myrtille looks away and says in a flat voice…
MYRTILLE: “Ok.”
MYRTILLE: “Too bad you didn’t get my riddle, but for me it’s a free ride.”
MYRTILLE: “I’m off. Lotsa people there tonight, and I don’t wanna end up sleeping on the street.”
MYRTILLE: “Take care, handsome!”
You start the engine right away. As you drive past the shelter, you see Myrtille amid some of her pals.
